Following arrows forward from C reaches E and then G, shown in the accent color with the edges used; D and F lie on another branch and are not reached. The card lists E, G." width="100%"} In a directed graph, the descendants of a node are all nodes it has a path *to*: its children, their children, and so on down to the leaves. In a dependency graph these are everything affected if the node changes; in a supply chain, every downstream stage; in a transmission network, everyone a case could have infected. The graph does not need to be acyclic. On an undirected graph, every other node in the same connected component counts as a descendant. The node itself is not included. For the reverse direction, see `ancestors()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node whose descendants to find, as an integer ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted IDs of the nodes reachable from `node=`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the label does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Changing `compile` in this build pipeline affects testing and packaging, but not the documentation, which only depends on the fetched source: ::: {#db537222 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["fetch", "compile", "test", "package", "docs"]) .add_edges([ ("fetch", "compile"), ("compile", "test"), ("test", "package"), ("compile", "package"), ("fetch", "docs"), ]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.descendants("compile")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['test', 'package'] ``` ::: :::
